# Welcome to WildPath

WildPath is a Foundry VTT system for the 2024 fifth-edition rules, with some of Baldur's Gate 3's flow. You click an Action, and the system resolves it: it rolls, applies damage and conditions, spends what it costs, and offers reactions.

This guide is in pages:

1. **Playing a turn**: the action bar, targets and areas, reactions, and chat cards.
2. **Your character**: leveling up, Heroic Inspiration, and languages.
3. **Books and homebrew**: content sources, your own books, the builder, and the Rules Inspector.
4. **GM tools**: rests, journeys, chases, Bastions, experience, crafting, traps and contagions.
5. **Exploring and gear**: carrying, coins, light, ammunition, poisons, scrolls and Bastions.
6. **Conditions and rules**: conditions beyond the core ones, contagions, and the 2014 rules.
7. **Settings reference**.

The system's content is the System Reference Document 5.2 (SRD 5.2) by Wizards of the Coast LLC, under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License. The books a GM owns can be added to a world for that GM's own table; they never ship with the system.

text.content:
The action bar

The action bar sits above Foundry's hotbar. It shows the creature whose Token you control, or else your assigned character.

  • Counters: your Action, Bonus Action, Reaction and movement, then pools such as Heroic Inspiration and Hit Dice.
  • Conditions: shown with their stacks. Hover one for its rules and the time it has left.
  • Groups: Actions, Bonus Actions, Reactions, Common, Items, then your spells by level.

To use an Action, target the creatures you mean with Foundry's targeting, then click its button.

  • Choices. An Action with choices asks them first. The dialog offers only what you can pay, and previews what it spends, the dice and the save. A spell also has small slot buttons that cast it at that level directly.
  • Areas.
  • For a sphere or other centred area, click where it centres.
  • For a cone or a line, click a corner on your Token's edge, then the direction.
  • Before you click, the creatures it would reach are outlined: allies in amber, others in red.
  • Escape or right-click cancels, and nothing is spent.
  • Greyed out. Hover a greyed-out button to see why: no slot left, an item not equipped or attuned, or it can't be used now. Spells you haven't prepared don't appear at all.

Common actions are in the Common group: Dash, Disengage, Dodge, Help, Hide, Grapple, Shove (Prone or Push), Unarmed Strike, Search, Study, Influence, Escape and Utilize. To Hide, you make a Stealth check against DC 15; on a success you become Invisible.

Reactions

Each reaction on the bar has a toggle that cycles through three policies:

  • Ask (the default): you are asked when it could be used.
  • Always: it is used for you, without asking.
  • Never: it is never offered.

A reaction is offered only when you can pay for it. Its prompt lists your options, with Decline chosen by default. Prompts have no time limit. If you're away, the GM can answer for you, and you'll see "The GM answered this for you."

Opportunity Attacks come built in. Every creature makes one with its first melee attack (or an Unarmed Strike) when a hostile creature leaves its reach during combat. Disengage prevents it. While you drag your Token, the ruler warns you of each Opportunity Attack your path would provoke. Its policy is in the Common group.

After an Action

Each Action posts one chat card: one row per target with its outcome (Hit, Critical hit, Miss, Saved, Failed save, Immune), and the rolls. Damage and misses also float over the Tokens. Reactions post cards of their own. If an Action can't be done, only you see why.

Odds. When targets are chosen, attack and save buttons can show the odds before you act, such as "56% to hit (+4 vs AC 15, disadvantage)". The GM always sees them. Players see them if the GM turns on Players see the odds, or against a creature an effect has revealed to them.

Dice

The GM picks digital or physical dice. With physical dice, you roll real dice and type in what they show:

  • for a d20 test, the natural d20;
  • with Advantage or Disadvantage, the higher or lower of your two d20s;
  • for damage, one total for each damage type.

A result the dice couldn't have given is asked for again.

text.content:
Leveling up

The level-up dialog opens when you drop a class, species or background on your sheet, or click Level up. It asks for:

  • that level's features;
  • your choices: skills, training, Weapon Mastery;
  • an Ability Score Improvement or a feat;
  • a subclass, or a species' size.

Confirm stays disabled until every choice is made, and closing the dialog changes nothing.

Hit Points. You get the Hit Die's maximum at level 1. After that, each level gives its average rounded up plus your Fortitude modifier, or a roll if the GM turned on Roll hit points on level up.

Experience. With experience points, your sheet shows your XP and the XP your next level needs. After a fight, the GM awards the defeated foes' XP, and the chat says when you may level up. With milestones, the GM tells you when.

Heroic Inspiration

You hold up to 4 Heroic Inspiration points, shown on your sheet and the bar; the GM awards them. When you miss an attack, fail a save or fail a check, you're asked whether to spend a point to reroll it. If the GM allows it, the GM may also spend one of your points to reroll a monster's d20.

Languages

Wrap words in a language's tag, such as [elvish]Well met[/elvish]. This works in chat, journals and speech bubbles, and the editor has a Language menu. In-character chat without a tag is Common.

Who reads it plainly:

  • the GM and its author;
  • anyone whose creature knows that language;
  • anyone under Comprehend Languages, Tongues or Telepathy.

Everyone else sees the same words in a historic script: Elvish in Tifinagh, Dwarvish in runes. A GM can choose fonts instead with Fonts for languages.

text.content:
What comes with the system

The compendiums hold the SRD 5.2: spells, equipment and features; classes, species and backgrounds; creatures; and the tables of its magic items. The WildPath Actions compendium holds sample Actions and the contagions' Infect Actions. This guide is the WildPath Guide compendium.

Content sources

Five world settings choose which sources' feats and subclasses the level-up dialog offers: 2014 core, 2024 core, supplements, Unearthed Arcana, and third-party or homebrew. All are on by default. They don't limit what you can browse in the compendiums.

Your own books

A GM who owns a dnd5e book module (a Player's Handbook, a Monster Manual) can convert it for their own world:

node scripts/content/convert-dnd5e-module.mjs <module-id> --srd <extracted dnd5e packs>

This writes a local module, wildpath-<module-id>, into your Foundry data, with that book's items and creatures; it only reads the source module. To use it, return to setup, launch the world, and enable it under Manage Modules. It is for your own table only: never share or publish it.

A book you own on paper can be typed in as JSON documents under <Foundry Data>/wildpath-sources/<book>/, then built into a local module with node scripts/content/build-local-module.mjs <book>. It counts as a supplement, or as third-party when the book is marked so.

The builder

An Action's sheet opens on its Builder tab, a set of tabletop questions: its cost, range, targets, area, attack, save or check, damage, healing and effects. Formulas like 2d6 + mod(wits) work. The Test tab previews the result, and the Advanced tab holds the raw data.

Other items have a Rules tab of rows: bonuses, Advantage or Disadvantage, resistances, speeds, light and more. Input that isn't valid isn't saved.

The Rules Inspector (GM)

Press Shift+I, or Inspect on a chat card, to see how the 25 most recent Actions resolved:

  • each stage they ran;
  • each roll, with its formula, Advantage or Disadvantage, natural result and total, and whether the dice were digital or physical;
  • attacks against AC and saves against DC;
  • health changes, payments, effects and errors.

It also shows whom an Action is waiting on, with Answer for them.

text.content:
These are for the GM. Most sit among the Token controls on the left of the canvas, as buttons.

Party Rest

Rests every player character at once: a Short Rest (1 hour) or a Long Rest (8 hours). Each character rests by its own rules: a Long Rest at 0 Hit Points gives no benefit, and a contagion may hold its Exhaustion. The world's time then moves on by those hours, so lit torches and other timed effects run out. Players spend their Hit Dice from their own sheets. If a rest is interrupted, decide whether to rest again.

Journey

The party travels some hours at a pace:

  • Fast, 4 miles an hour: Disadvantage on Perception and Survival checks.
  • Normal, 3 miles an hour.
  • Slow, 2 miles an hour: Advantage on Perception and Survival checks.

Each player character gets the pace's effect for those hours. Every hour past 8 is a forced march: each character makes a Fortitude save, DC 10 + 1 for each hour past 8, and gains 1 Exhaustion level on a failure. Time moves on, and the chat says how far the party went. Navigation, foraging and terrain are yours to judge.

Chase

Turns the running combat into a chase; press it again to end the chase.

  • Each creature Dashes 3 + its Fortitude modifier times freely.
  • Each Dash beyond that takes a DC 10 Fortitude check, and a failure gives 1 Exhaustion level.
  • At the end of each turn a d20 is rolled. On 10 or lower you are told a complication befalls that creature; you decide what it is.

Bastion Turn

Moves the world 7 days on.

  • Each player character's special facilities carry out the orders issued on its sheet's Bastion section.
  • Craft works 7 days on the Item dropped on the facility, and makes it (paying its materials) when its days are done.
  • Trade buys stock with the character's gold, or sells what it holds at its profit.
  • Recruit adds up to 4 Bastion Defenders, as many as the facilities house.
  • Empower, Harvest and Research are listed; the facility's text says what you give.
  • The chat lists each order carried out.
  • A character whose facilities all maintained has a Bastion event: drawn from the DMG's "Bastion Events" table when its converted module is enabled, else a d100. An Attack removes a defender for each 1 on 6d6; any other event is yours to run.
  • Every order then goes back to Maintain.

On a character's Bastion map, the Make a Scene button builds a Scene of it: each facility coloured and named, walls around them. Add the doors.

Encounters and experience

  • Difficulty. The combat tracker names the difficulty of the combat being viewed: its hostile creatures' XP against the player characters' budgets (2024 Low, Moderate and High).
  • Awarding XP. With Level Advancement set to experience points, ending a combat offers the XP of the hostile creatures it defeated, split evenly among the player characters. The chat names anyone who may now level up.

Making and crafting items

  • Craft for a character. Open an item's sheet and choose this button. You pick a player character, it pays the materials from its coins, and it gains the item. The chat says how many days of work it took. By the 2024 rules:
  • a mundane item takes half its price and a day for each 10 GP of it;
  • a magic item takes its rarity's days and gold (half for a consumable);
  • a Spell Scroll takes its spell level's.
  • Make Spell Scroll. This button is on any spell's sheet. It puts a Spell Scroll of that spell in the Items directory.
  • Its reader casts the spell at its own level, with the scroll's save DC and attack bonus.
  • A reader whose highest spell level is below the spell's first makes a check, DC 10 + the spell's level, and loses the spell on a failure.
  • Either way, the scroll crumbles.
  • Identified. A magic item's sheet has an Identified box and an unidentified name. While the box is unticked, players see only the item's unidentified name and description.

Traps, poisons and contagions

  • Traps. Each trap tier is an Action. Give it to a creature you control (a "Dungeon" NPC with a Token works) and use it to set the trap: a lasting 5-foot square anywhere. It springs its save or attack on each creature entering it. Delete its Region when it is found and disarmed.
  • Contagions. "Infect: Cackle Fever", "Infect: Sewer Plague" and "Infect: Sight Rot" are in the WildPath Actions compendium.
  • A failed save infects the creature, and its incubation is rolled.
  • When enough of the world's time has passed, its symptoms start.
  • After each Long Rest its creature saves against it.
  • Surprised. Mark a creature Surprised from its Token HUD. It rolls initiative with Disadvantage, and the condition ends after that roll.

Lair Actions

A creature with Lair Actions gets its Lair Action back at the top of each round, before anyone acts, and you are whispered who may take one.

text.content:
Carrying

The world's Carrying setting decides what a character's load does.

  • Carrying capacity (the 2024 rule, the default): a character carries up to its Might score × 15 lb, more for a larger creature. If it carries more, its Speed is at most 5 feet.
  • Variant encumbrance: over 5 × Might the character is Encumbered (−10 feet of Speed). Over 10 × Might it is Heavily Encumbered (−20 feet, and Disadvantage on Might, Agility and Fortitude d20 tests).
  • Off: weight is only shown.

The sheet's gear list shows what you carry against your capacity, and what the load does to you.

Coins

Your coins (PP, GP, EP, SP, CP) are with your gear on the sheet. Crafting pays from them and makes change.

Light

To light a Torch, Candle, Lamp or Lantern, use its Light Action. A Torch or Candle lights with a Bonus Action. Your Token then sheds the item's light for its hours: a Torch gives Bright Light 20 feet and Dim Light 20 feet more, and a Bullseye Lantern shines a cone.

Ammunition

A weapon with the Ammunition property needs ammunition of its kind in your gear: Arrows for a bow, Bolts for a crossbow, Bullets for a sling. Each attack spends one, and with none left the attack is refused. After a fight, the GM may let you recover half of what you spent.

Poisons

  • Contact, ingested and inhaled poisons: using one is the Utilize action on a creature within 5 feet, which saves against it.
  • Injury poisons: using one coats your weapon for 1 minute. Your next weapon hit offers the poison's save to the creature you hit, and that uses up the coat.

Spell Scrolls

A Spell Scroll in your gear gives you its spell's Action. If you can't cast spells, you can't read it. If the spell's level is above what you can cast, you first make a check with your spellcasting ability, DC 10 + its level, and lose the spell on a failure. Either way, the scroll crumbles once read.

Unidentified items

Until your GM says you've identified a magic item, you see only what it looks like: its unidentified name and description, also on the Actions it gives you.

Bastions

From level 5 a character may have a Bastion. Its facilities are listed in the Bastion section of your sheet. Before each Bastion turn, issue each special facility its order there; the GM runs the turn.

  • Facilities. Drop a facility on your sheet. A special one needs its level and a free slot (2 at level 5, 4 at 9, 5 at 13, 6 at 17); the sheet shows how many you use. Your first two basic facilities are free; more cost gold, as does Enlarge.
  • Crafting. Drop an Item on a facility that crafts (a Smithy, a Workshop) to choose what its Craft orders make.
  • Defenders. The sheet shows your Bastion Defenders and how many your facilities house.
  • The map. Bastion map opens a grid of 5-foot squares, 12 by 12 at level 5, growing to 24 by 24 at 17. Pick a facility, then click or drag over squares to lay it out in any shape, up to its space (Cramped 4 squares, Roomy 16, Vast 36). Right-click clears a square. Save the map when it has no problems listed.

## Poisons

- **Contact, ingested and inhaled poisons**: using one is the Utilize action on a creature within 5 feet, which saves against it.
- **Injury poisons**: using one coats your weapon for 1 minute. Your next weapon hit offers the poison's save to the creature you hit, and that uses up the coat.

## Spell Scrolls

A Spell Scroll in your gear gives you its spell's Action. If you can't cast spells, you can't read it. If the spell's level is above what you can cast, you first make a check with your spellcasting ability, DC 10 + its level, and lose the spell on a failure. Either way, the scroll crumbles once read.

## Unidentified items

Until your GM says you've identified a magic item, you see only what it looks like: its unidentified name and description, also on the Actions it gives you.

## Bastions

From level 5 a character may have a Bastion. Its facilities are listed in the **Bastion** section of your sheet. Before each Bastion turn, issue each special facility its order there; the GM runs the turn.

- **Facilities.** Drop a facility on your sheet. A special one needs its level and a free slot (2 at level 5, 4 at 9, 5 at 13, 6 at 17); the sheet shows how many you use. Your first two basic facilities are free; more cost gold, as does **Enlarge**.
- **Crafting.** Drop an Item on a facility that crafts (a Smithy, a Workshop) to choose what its Craft orders make.
- **Defenders.** The sheet shows your Bastion Defenders and how many your facilities house.
- **The map.** **Bastion map** opens a grid of 5-foot squares, 12 by 12 at level 5, growing to 24 by 24 at 17. Pick a facility, then click or drag over squares to lay it out in any shape, up to its space (Cramped 4 squares, Roomy 16, Vast 36). Right-click clears a square. **Save the map** when it has no problems listed.

World settings, under Game Settings → Configure Settings → WildPath. The GM sets them.

SettingWhat it does
RulesWhich edition's conditions and rules apply: 2024 (the default) or 2014. Takes effect after a reload.
DiceHow rolls are made: digitally, or with physical dice whose totals the roller types in.
Movement MeasurementWhether a turn's movement is counted as distance on the Scene or as grid spaces crossed.
Several saves at onceWhen many creatures save at once: one window for all of them, or every save rolled for you.
Players see the oddsHouse rule: players see their chance to hit and a target's chance to fail its save before acting.
GM may reroll monster rolls with players' inspirationThe GM may spend a player character's Heroic Inspiration to reroll a monster's d20.
Roll hit points on level upRoll each new level's Hit Die, or take its average (the 2024 default).
Shove as a Bonus ActionBaldur's Gate 3's rule: Shove costs a Bonus Action instead of an Action.
High groundBaldur's Gate 3's rule: +2 to attacks from 8 feet or more above the target, −2 from 8 feet below.
CarryingThe 2024 carrying capacity, the variant encumbrance, or off. Takes effect after a reload.
Level AdvancementBy experience points (offered when a combat ends) or by milestones.
Offer 2014 core content, 2024 core content, supplements, Unearthed Arcana, third-party and homebrew contentWhich sources' feats and subclasses the level-up dialog offers.
Fonts for languagesA font for a language its reader doesn't know, instead of its script (dwarvish=Dethek). Add the font files first, under Additional Fonts.
